Diego / team —

I've reviewed Skyward's annotated SLA. Below are proposed redlines and rationale to keep the commercial exposure manageable while addressing the customer's asks: 

1) Uptime target (Section 2.1): Acceptable approach — allow 99.98% for a Dedicated footprint only. Add explicit language: "Customer may elect Dedicated capacity; 99.98% uptime is available only for dedicated instances provisioned and paid in accordance with the Dedicated Order Form. Hosted instances will remain at 99.95%." Rationale: limits exposure on shared infrastructure.

2) Service credits (Section 3): Replace current stacking language with a single net-credit formula. Proposed wording: "Service Credits are calculated on a per-billing-period basis and shall not be cumulative for the same underlying root cause. Where multiple outages arise from distinct root causes, credits may be applied separately, subject to the aggregate cap set forth in the Order Form." Rationale: avoids double recovery for the same event, provides clarity for multiple distinct events.

3) Planned maintenance (Section 4): Accept 72-hour notice for routine maintenance. For the "quarterly 6-hour blackout" request: propose compromise — allow one scheduled maintenance window up to 6 hours per calendar quarter with prior written approval and an advance notice of not less than 7 days; if unapproved, normal credit rules apply. Rationale: limits unilateral scheduling that could impact multi-tenant operations.

4) Measurement and proof (Section 5): Add a clause for mutual measurement and evidence exchange: "Customer and Redwood will exchange outage logs and measurement methodology upon request for credit adjudication." Keep standard dispute resolution process.

5) Remedies cap: Propose keeping aggregate annual credit cap at 50% of fees for the impacted service; if the customer insists on higher uptime with a lower cap, escalate to CRO for approval.

I attached a tracked changes extract in the Drive folder (link below) and a plain-text redline if you prefer to paste into the order form. If sales wants to proceed with a Dedicated commitment to achieve 99.98%, we need a commercial addendum with committed monthly spend and term.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
